item.title: Yemen's Houthis escalate deadly attacks on Saudi-backed troops
item.description: Yemen's Houthi rebels launch fresh attacks on Saudi-backed government troops, says Yemeni state media, as Cruz says Trump must seek "regime collapse."

item.title: More than 50 decomposing bodies found at Far South Side funeral home
item.description: An investigation was underway at a Far South Side funeral home after more than 50 decomposing bodies were found in the facility.

item.title: At least 6 dead in Thailand high school shooting after suspect kills grandparents
item.description: A teenager described as "troubled" by a classmate killed his grandparents before gunning down at least six more people at a school in Thailand, police said.

item.title: These NYC centers allow hard drug use in-house. Nearly 5 years in, is it helping?
item.description: An addiction-services nonprofit approved by the city focuses on harm reduction for hard drug users — to the chagrin of some in the neighborhood.

item.title: Sen. Cruz calls for Trump to arm Iranian protesters: "Our objective should be regime collapse"
item.description: As the U.S. angles for a deal with Iran, Republican Sen. Ted Cruz told Aaron MacLean on the "School of War" podcast that President Trump should heap more pressure on Iran's regime — including by arming Iranians to "let them overthrow their own government."

item.title: Trump to announce $180 million to boost mining education
item.description: President Trump is planning to announce over $180 million in grants to boost educational programs for the mining industry, CBS News has learned, part of a bid to increase critical mineral production.

item.title: Cruz calls for Trump to arm Iranians: "Our objective should be regime collapse"
item.description: GOP Sen. Ted Cruz told Aaron MacLean on the "School of War" podcast that President Trump should heap more pressure on Iran — including by arming Iranians to "let them overthrow their own government."

item.title: Iran, Oman deal on Strait of Hormuz getting close, Tehran says
item.description: Iran and Oman are close to agreeing on new arrangements for the Strait of Hormuz, but not for a full reopening of the vital waterway, Iran's state news agency says.

item.title: Trump-endorsed Rep. Andy Ogles projected to lose GOP primary in Tennessee
item.description: Two-term Rep. Andy Ogles lost the Republican primary for his Tennessee House seat, the Associated Press projects, despite securing an endorsement from President Trump.

item.title: U.S. Marine vet, detained in Russia since 2022, hospitalized in serious condition
item.description: Robert Gilman, 32, is being held at a Russian hospital in what his advocate, Eric Lebson of Global Reach, described as a "dissociative stupor."

item.title: FAA orders inspections of 737 Max jets after cracks found in older planes
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration has ordered inspections of hundreds of Boeing 737 Max jets after cracks were found in parts of some older model Boeing planes.

item.title: Minnesota Chipotle burrito bowl meal led to sepsis hospitalization, lawsuit says
item.description: A Minnesota woman says she fainted, spiked a 102-degree fever, and was hospitalized with sepsis three days after eating a chicken burrito bowl at a Chipotle in Roseville, and genetic testing connected her case to a multistate outbreak, according to a lawsuit filed Tuesday.

item.title: Sen. Marsha Blackburn wins Republican primary for Tennessee governor
item.description: Sen. Marsha Blackburn had faced two primary challengers, including Rep. John Rose.

item.title: Court orders Meta and Instagram to pay $567M to address kids' mental health
item.description: A New Mexico court has ordered Instagram and Facebook parent company Meta to pay $567 million to address harms to young people from its platforms.

item.title: Marking 61 years since Voting Rights Act was signed
item.description: Sixty-one years ago, President Lyndon B. Johnson signed the Voting Rights Act into law, helping advance equal access to the ballot box by banning racial discrimination. Now, court rulings, new election laws and federal policy proposals are renewing questions about voter access. Election law expert and CBS News contributor David Becker has more.

item.title: Louisiana reports 5 deaths, 9 cases of flesh-eating bacteria
item.description: As the summer season continues to bring people to the beach, the Louisiana Health Department warns to take precautions against a potentially fatal flesh-eating bacteria found in warm coastal waters. Officials confirmed nine cases this year and five deaths.

item.title: Pro Football Hall of Fame Game kicks off 2026 NFL preseason
item.description: The 2026 NFL preseason kicks off Thursday night as the Carolina Panthers take on the Arizona Cardinals in the annual Hall of Fame Game. Zack Rosenblatt, senior NFL writer for the Athletic, joins CBS News to discuss the game and the upcoming season.

item.title: More kids ditching their phones to find summer jobs
item.description: Meet the children leaving their devices behind this summer to flex their entrepreneurial muscles with summer jobs.

item.title: Trump issues new executive orders aimed at birthright citizenship
item.description: The Supreme Court in June struck down President Trump's earlier executive order aimed at ending birthright citizenship.

item.title: Centrist Democrat group plans $15 million effort against Democratic Socialists of America
item.description: Republicans running against democratic socialists have found an unlikely ally: other Democrats. The centrist Democrat think tank Third Way has pledged $15 million to discredit the DSA movement between now and 2028. Third Way President Jonathan Cowan joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Paul skipped full Senate vote for Fauci contempt push, an "unusual maneuver," former DOJ lawyer says
item.description: A Senate committee on Thursday voted to hold Dr. Anthony Fauci in contempt for refusing last week to answer questions related to government actions during the COVID-19 pandemic. Former Deputy Assistant Attorney General Tom Dupree joins to discuss.

item.title: 8/6: CBS Evening News
item.description: Boeing planes to be inspected for cracks; Trump signs new birthright citizenship orders.

item.title: Stevens says of El-Sayed: "Differences were aired out"
item.description: Though Rep. Haley Stevens stressed a unified front moving forward, she was evasive on whether she would appear with El-Sayed on the campaign trail.

item.title: Bessent announces crackdown on undocumented immigrants' use of U.S. banks
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Arizona bankers the administration won't allow "risks posed by the extension of financial services to illegal aliens."

item.title: Flesh-eating bacteria have killed 5 in Louisiana this year, officials say
item.description: A flesh-eating bacterium found in warm coastal waters is responsible for at least five deaths so far this year in Louisiana, state health officials reported Thursday.

item.title: Stevens on backing El-Sayed after primary loss: "I am going to be a part of stopping MAGA and Trump"
item.description: Rep. Haley Stevens just lost a very close Michigan Democratic Senate primary to progressive Abdul El-Sayed. She's endorsed him, but questions persist about Democratic unity. Stevens joins "The Takeout" in her first television interview since her defeat.

item.title: America's water systems are getting hacked amid security gaps, experts say
item.description: The nation's 152,000 public water systems often lack defenses against malicious actors, cybersecurity experts said. Here's what to know.

item.title: Mitch McConnell says he's been discharged from rehab
item.description: Republican Sen. Mitch McConnell of Kentucky was hospitalized on June 14.

item.title: DOGE's "wall of receipts" riddled with inaccuracies, GAO says
item.description: The Government Accountability Office found that DOGE overestimated its savings, among other issues.

item.title: Trump voter pleads for fiancée's release after ICE arrest: "They're destroying families"
item.description: "They are picking up law-abiding citizens. They're destroying families, jobs," said a Texas man who regrets his vote for President Trump after his fiancée, an immigrant from Venezuela, was detained by ICE.
